title: Mailbox wake transition owner with persisted obligation and attempt identities, and a durable attempt fence before the runtime send
outcome:
One session-owned transition owner (a reducer over session state) is the only way a mailbox wake's ownership changes: accept, coalesce, promote, arm and confirm. Each accepted wake carries a durable obligation identity with its frozen scope. Each promotion carries a fresh durable attempt identity: re-promoting the same sequence is a new attempt, and one attempt's evidence never classifies another. Before a mailbox turn can reach the runtime, its exact attempt crosses a durability fence. The fence is waited off StateInner, following the Engram admission PersistFence pattern; if persistence is missing or uncertain, the send is withheld. Queue and active ownership are replaced in one persisted session image; no path pops a wake and leaves only a stack-local boundary.

Provenance: Architect2's structural decision f639826d on w-3bd74078208d (item 1 of the decomposition the holder Termal::Opus3 proposed in TermAl mailbox 03723eab #42; Fable2 accepted it in #43). Read-only facts: commit_locked only queues for the persist worker, and no revision fence exists (sse_broadcast.rs:80, persist_fence.rs:8-19). active_turn_generation is not persisted (persisted_state.rs:521). MailboxNotificationDelivery has no attempt id (runtime.rs:553).
Review findings it carries: round-3 Low (Claude, delegation-34e81e3e): a stale handoffAttempted mark left by a rejected or superseded attempt makes boot hold a re-promoted, never-sent continuation as unknown, because the attempt is not identified.
Design of the mailbox wake: docs/features/agent-mailboxes.md. Criteria to be proposed by the holder and concurred by the coordinator.
acceptance: Mailbox wake transition owner with persisted obligation and attempt identities, and a durable attempt fence before the runtime send is done
